newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil seen earning $10 bln with global shr offers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil seen earning $10 bln with global shr offers.

text.p: The vice-president of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), Jose Pio Borges, said Brazil was expected to earn $10 billion from global share offers in 1997, up from $500 million over the past two years.
Borges told reporters this estimate by foreign investment banks included global offers of shares in privatized electricity firm Light, privatized mining giant CVRD and private bank Unibanco.
The Light and CVRD offers will take place in the second half of this year.

He also said the federal government was expected to earn 30 billion reais ($28.04 billion) each from the privatization of the electricity and telecommunications sectors over the next three years and state governments would take in another 15 billion reais with the sale of their power firms.

He said either Furnas or Eletrosul would be the first sold with the respective tender documents due to be published by the end of this year. Consultants are expected to have contracts by the end of May to decide which of the two electricity generators will be privatized first.
Borges said a controling stake in Minas Gerais state power utility Cemig -- worth 1.1 billion reais -- which was due to be auctioned on May 6, would probably now be sold within the next two months.
The sale had been delayed because companies pre-qualified for the auction asked for more time to visit the firm.
Borges expected the telecommunications law, which sets out the rules for the privatization of the sector to be approved by Congress still in the first half of 1997.

Once the legislation is passed, the BNDES will issue contracts to three sets of consultants to create a model for the regulatory body of the sector; to draw up the privatization rules and to evaluate and sell the companies.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
